claims.text: High-temperature sliding of FeNiCrCoCu coatings dynamically forms an ultra-nanocrystalline and/or partially amorphous near-surface layer.
The dynamically refined near-surface layer governs the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu coatings.
The refined layer reduces shear strength and friction.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse or conventional grain structure.
Controlled pre-annealing alters the coating's initial grain-size distribution.
The proposed wear regime is approximately 300°C to 600°C under high cyclic sliding loads.
Elevated temperature and high shear cause dynamic recrystallization and/or amorphization in the FeNiCrCoCu coating subsurface.
Inverse Hall-Petch behavior makes further grain refinement lower the shear strength of the refined surface layer.
Lower shear strength consequently decreases the coefficient of friction.
Reduced friction suppresses crack initiation and propagation.
Formation of the low-friction refined layer improves overall wear resistance.
Coatings that dynamically refine during high-temperature wear will have lower wear rates and coefficients of friction than untreated baseline coatings.
Lower wear and friction will coincide with an observable transition to an ultrafine near-surface microstructure.
Pre-annealed fine-grained coatings may reach optimal wear resistance after a shorter transient period.
The proposed beneficial effect occurs specifically within about 300°C to 600°C.
The effect requires sliding loads sufficient to trigger dynamic microstructural evolution and ceases beyond conditions causing severe oxidation or melting.

contradictions.description: The intervention and falsification design compare pre-annealed and untreated coatings under the same high-temperature tests, whereas the stated baseline includes room- or low-temperature testing. Using temperature and pretreatment differences simultaneously would confound the intervention comparison.
